map.根据试样受热前后的长度变化计算收缩率，结合收缩温度评估皮革热稳定性与鞣制效果，是: Computes the shrinkage rate from the length change of the specimen before and after heating, and combines it with shrinkage temperature to assess thermal stability and tanning quality — a common calculation tool for leather heat-resistance and tanning quality testing.
map.测定皮革受热后的收缩率与收缩温度，评估鞣制程度与热稳定性。: Measures the shrinkage rate and shrinkage temperature of leather after heating to assess the degree of tanning and thermal stability.
map.用收缩温度判断铬鞣是否充分（铬鞣革一般要求 ≥95℃）。: Use shrinkage temperature to judge whether chrome tanning is complete (chrome-tanned leather generally requires ≥95 °C).
map.对比不同鞣制工艺或批次的热稳定性，排查鞣制不足问题。: Compare thermal stability across tanning processes or batches to catch under-tanning.
map.：收缩率 = (受热前长度 − 受热后长度) ÷ 受热前长度 × 100%。热稳: : shrinkage rate = (length before − length after) ÷ length before × 100%. Thermal stability grading: <3% excellent, 3%–5% good, 5%–10% fair, ≥10% poor. Shrinkage temperature reading: ≥95 °C meets chrome-tanned leather requirements; 80–95 °C suggests incomplete tanning; <80 °C needs stronger tanning.
map.：试样原长 100.0 mm、受热后 96.5 mm：收缩率 = (100−96: : for a specimen originally 100.0 mm shrinking to 96.5 mm, the rate = (100−96.5)/100×100 = 3.5%, rated "good"; if the shrinkage temperature also measures 98 °C, tanning is complete and stability good. A 12% shrinkage with only 82 °C indicates insufficient tanning needing a top-up.
map.收缩温度为什么能反映鞣制程度？: Why Does Shrinkage Temperature Reflect the Degree of Tanning?
map.鞣制使胶原纤维产生交联，交联越充分、受热收缩所需的能量越高，收缩温度越高；因此它: Tanning cross-links collagen fibers; the more complete the cross-linking, the more energy is needed to shrink on heating, so the shrinkage temperature rises. It is therefore the most direct thermal indicator of tanning quality.
map.收缩率和收缩温度要一起看吗？: Should the Shrinkage Rate and Temperature Be Read Together?
map.要。收缩温度反映“何时开始收缩”，收缩率反映“收缩多少”；可能出现温度达标但收缩: Yes. Shrinkage temperature shows when contraction starts, the rate shows how much it contracts; you can have an acceptable temperature but excessive contraction, so read them together.
